subject.title: fix(models): clear stale auth cooldowns after early limit resets

question: Should OpenClaw make `models auth clear-cooldown <profile-id>` a supported public recovery contract for early provider billing or usage recovery, rather than pursuing an automatic probe or cooldown-policy change?
rationale: The implementation is additive but exposes a durable CLI and operator workflow that changes how users recover provider availability; tests cannot establish that this is the intended long-term product boundary.

options.title: Adopt the manual recovery command
options.body: Approve this narrowly scoped CLI contract after complete real-flow proof shows that it clears only persisted health state and safely returns the recovered profile to routing.

options.title: Prefer automatic recovery
options.body: Keep the issue focused on provider probing or a bounded cooldown policy instead of adding a user-operated reset command.

options.title: Defer the product surface
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers choose a broader provider-recovery policy and ownership boundary.

recommendation.title: Adopt the manual recovery command
recommendation.body: Approve this narrowly scoped CLI contract after complete real-flow proof shows that it clears only persisted health state and safely returns the recovered profile to routing.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision belongs with the people currently responsible for auth-profile persistence and provider-routing behavior; the available evidence does not safely identify an individual.
